A 46-year-old homeless man is brought to the emergency department after being found intoxicated. His
medical history includes IV drug use, diabetes, alcohol abuse, and malnutrition, with prior
hospitalizations for pancreatitis and sepsis. On arrival, he is minimally responsive, withdrawing only to
painful stimuli. His vital signs are: temperature 98.1°F (37.5°C), blood pressure 105/53 mmHg, pulse
147/min, respirations 13/min, and oxygen saturation 95% on room air. Physical examination reveals
tachycardia, a diastolic murmur at the left lower sternal border, and bilateral pulmonary crackles. He is
started on IV fluids, vancomycin, and piperacillin-tazobactam. Initial laboratory results are as follows: -
Hemoglobin: 9 g/dL - Hematocrit: 30% - Leukocyte count: 11,500/mm³ (normal differential) - Platelet
count: 297,000/mm³ - Serum: Na■: 139 mEq/L, Cl■: 100 mEq/L, K■: 4.0 mEq/L, HCO■■: 28 mEq/L,
BUN: 33 mg/dL, Glucose: 60 mg/dL, Creatinine: 1.7 mg/dL, Ca²■: 9.7 mg/dL - PT: 20 seconds, aPTT:
60 seconds - AST: 1,010 U/L, ALT: 950 U/L After five days of treatment, the patient’s neurological
status improves. His updated vital signs are: temperature 99.5°F (37.5°C), blood pressure 130/90
mmHg, pulse 90/min, respirations 11/min, and oxygen saturation 99% on room air. Repeat laboratory
results are as follows: - Hemoglobin: 10 g/dL - Hematocrit: 32% - Leukocyte count: 9,500/mm³ (normal
differential) - Platelet count: 199,000/mm³ - Serum: Na■: 140 mEq/L, Cl■: 102 mEq/L, K■: 4.3 mEq/L,
HCO■■: 24 mEq/L, BUN: 31 mg/dL, Glucose: 100 mg/dL, Creatinine: 1.6 mg/dL, Ca²■: 9.0 mg/dL -
PT: 50 seconds, aPTT: 110 seconds - AST: 150 U/L, ALT: 90 U/L Which of the following best describes
the patient’s current condition? Answer Choices: (A) Alcoholic hepatitis with coagulopathy (B) Acute
pancreatitis with hepatic involvement (C) Subacute bacterial endocarditis progression (D) Multiorgan
dysfunction syndrome (E) Early septic shock resolution (F) Acute renal failure (G) Recovery from
ischemic liver disease (H) Fulminant liver failure (I) Compensated disseminated intravascular
coagulation (J) Recovery from acute renal failure
